_meta.indication: TRESIBA is a long-acting human insulin analog indicated to improve glycemic control in adults with diabetes mellitus

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study A (Trial NN1250-3583), type 1 diabetes pivotal trial
pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 3 pivotal efficacy and safety trial for IDeg U100 formulation
pivotal_trials.design: 52-week randomized, open-label, multicenter, treat-to-target, non-inferiority trial; TRESIBA once-daily vs insulin glargine U-100, both with mealtime insulin aspart
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus on a basal-bolus insulin regimen
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: change in HbA1c from baseline to end of treatment (week 52), tested for non-inferiority (margin 0.4%)
pivotal_trials.result: At week 52 the estimated treatment difference in HbA1c reduction (TRESIBA minus insulin glargine U-100) was -0.01% (95% CI -0.14% to 0.11%), meeting the pre-specified non-inferiority margin of 0.4%

nct_ctgov.title: Comparison of NN1250 Plus Insulin Aspart With Insulin Glargine Plus Insulin Aspart in Type 1 Diabetes

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study D (type 2 diabetes pivotal trial, add-on to metformin ± DPP-4 inhibitor in insulin-naive adults)
pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 3 therapeutic confirmatory (pivotal) efficacy and safety trial
pivotal_trials.design: 52-week randomized, open-label, multicenter, treat-to-target, non-inferiority trial; TRESIBA once-daily vs insulin glargine U-100, on background metformin alone or with a DPP-4 inhibitor
pivotal_trials.population: Insulin-naive adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus inadequately controlled on one or more oral antidiabetic agents
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: change in HbA1c from baseline to end of treatment (week 52), tested for non-inferiority (margin 0.4%)
pivotal_trials.result: At week 52 the estimated treatment difference in HbA1c reduction (TRESIBA minus insulin glargine U-100) was 0.09% (95% CI -0.04% to 0.22%), meeting the pre-specified non-inferiority margin of 0.4%

key_safety: Hypoglycemia is the most common adverse reaction and may be life-threatening. Other common adverse reactions include allergic reactions, injection site reactions, lipodystrophy, pruritus, rash, edema and weight gain. Among non-hypoglycemia adverse reactions occurring in ≥5% of patients, nasopharyngitis had the highest rate in both populations: 23.9% in type 1 diabetes and 12.9% in type 2 diabetes. A signal of serious cardiovascular risk was also identified.
target_moa: Insulin degludec is a long-acting basal human insulin analog whose primary activity is regulation of glucose metabolism; it lowers blood glucose by stimulating peripheral glucose uptake (skeletal muscle and fat) and inhibiting hepatic glucose production, and it forms multi-hexamers on subcutaneous injection to produce a long, flat glucose-lowering effect

summary.text: TRESIBA was submitted as a 505(b)(1) NDA received September 29, 2011. Approval was refused on the first cycle via a Complete Response Letter dated 8 February 2013 (manufacturing deficiencies plus a cardiovascular safety signal). After an End-of-Review meeting, the sponsor filed a Class 2 resubmission on 26 March 2015 with reassuring interim results from the dedicated DEVOTE cardiovascular outcomes trial, leading to approval on September 25, 2015; FDA additionally required completion of the DEVOTE CVOT as a post-marketing requirement (PMR 2954-2).

requirement.text: 2954-2: Conduct a randomized, double-blind, active-controlled trial evaluating the effect of Tresiba on the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus, to demonstrate that the upper bound of the 2-sided 95% CI for the risk ratio of adjudicated MACE (non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke, CV death) vs comparator is less than 1.3

citations.quote: 2954-2 Conduct a randomized, double-blind, active-controlled trial evaluating the effect of Tresiba (insulin degludec injection) on the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus. The primary objective of the trial should be to demonstrate that the upper bound of the 2-sided 95% confidence interval for the estimated risk ratio comparing the incidence of adjudicated MACE (non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, cardiovascular death) observed with Tresiba to that observed in the comparator group is less than 1.3.
